samples.summary: Esc handler is a bare window listener, so closing an overlay (ShareDialog, Select popover) with Esc also navigates the user out of the image viewer
samples.evidence: image-viewer.tsx:113-130 registers `keydown` on `window` and now does `else if (e.key === "Escape" && onClose) onClose()`. The only guard is `t.tagName === INPUT/TEXTAREA || isContentEditable`. The image layout renders `<ShareDialog documentId={documentId} />` (file-detail.tsx:148), a Radix Dialog whose DismissableLayer closes on Escape via a document-level keydown; the event target is the focused DialogContent/SelectContent `div`, not an input, so the viewer's handler also fires. Pressing Esc once to dismiss the share dialog (or a Select dropdown inside it) therefore closes the overlay AND navigates to the documents list, losing the viewer. No `e.defaultPrevented` check, no open-overlay check, and no `stopPropagation` from the dialog prevents this.

samples.summary: useDocumentsPath returns "/documents" while the workspaces query is still in flight, so an early Esc/back-button press lands on the wrong list
samples.evidence: `const { data: workspaces = [] } = useQuery(...)` defaults to `[]` during loading, so `slug` is undefined and the hook returns "/documents" until the request resolves. `close` in ImageFileLayout (file-detail.tsx:131-134) captures that value, so an Esc or back-button click within the first moments of mount navigates to the workspace-less list instead of `/w/<slug>`. Previously the only consumer of this fallback was the error redirect in FileShell, which fires after fetches; the new user-triggered paths can fire immediately. A loading-state guard (skip/disable navigation until `isSuccess`) would avoid the wrong destination.

samples.summary: No test exercises Esc while a dialog/popover overlay is open, the case where the new global handler misbehaves
samples.evidence: The three cases cover window-target Esc, input-target Esc, and the tokened mount. Nothing renders the viewer inside the real FileShell/ShareDialog composition, so the double-handling in the overlay case (finding above) is untested. Also note the `token` case only asserts `not.toThrow()`, which would pass even if `onClose` semantics regressed.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. image-viewer.tsx:113-130 attaches a bubble-phase `keydown` listener on `window` whose only bail-out is INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable targets (lines 116-123), then calls `onClose()` on Escape (line 126) with no `defaultPrevented` or open-overlay check. file-detail.tsx:136-153 mounts `<ShareDialog>` (line 148) in the same layout as `<ImageViewer onClose={close}>` (line 152), where `close` navigates away (lines 131-134). share-dialog.tsx:155-273 is a Radix Dialog containing two Radix Selects and supplies no `onEscapeKeyDown`/`stopPropagation`; ui/dialog.tsx:47-71 forwards props to `DialogPrimitive.Content` untouched, and a repo-wide grep for stopPropagation/onEscapeKeyDown/defaultPrevented finds nothing in the dialog or select path. Radix dismisses via a document-level handler without stopping propagation, so the event reaches the window listener; focus while the dialog/select is open is on a button or the SelectContent div, so the INPUT/TEXTAREA guard does not apply. Pressing Esc once therefore closes the overlay AND navigates out of the viewer — a real missing-guard logic bug on a reachable path, in the correctness lane.
